summary: Backend + frontend E2E testing for Work Shifts, Payroll, Notifications, and public-signup lockdown. 14/14 backend pytest tests pass. All primary frontend flows verified: admin sidebar shows 'Work Shifts' (no 'Tasks'), employee sees 'My Shifts', /register redirects to /login, login page has 'Contact your administrator' (no signup link), notification bell shows shift_cancelled notification for admin, Assign Shift dialog opens with all required fields (employee select, in-office/WFH toggle, start/end pickers, Mon-Sun chips, date range), Payroll page renders + Create Payroll dialog present, employee shift card exposes Join Work + a (icon-only) cancel button.

critical.issue: When called by an authenticated admin to create another user, the endpoint sets access_token/refresh_token cookies on the RESPONSE for the newly created user. This overwrites the admin's own session cookies in the browser, effectively logging the admin out and logging them in as the new employee. Fix: only set cookies when there is no current authenticated user (i.e., true self-signup path). For admin-initiated creation, skip response.set_cookie calls.

issues: Stat card still labeled 'Active Tasks' and Quick Action still shows 'Assign Task' / 'In office or work from home'. Since Tasks were renamed to Work Shifts, these labels should be updated to 'Active Shifts' and 'Assign Shift' respectively to be consistent with the sidebar and new terminology.
Cancel Shift button on shift card is icon-only (red X), which is not discoverable. Consider adding a tooltip (title='Cancel Shift') or the text label to match the spec.

action_items: Fix /api/auth/register to not overwrite the caller's cookies when the request is made by an authenticated admin (only set cookies for anonymous self-signup path, which is currently disabled anyway).
Update admin Dashboard quick actions/stat cards: 'Assign Task' -> 'Assign Shift', 'Active Tasks' -> 'Active Shifts' to complete Task->Work Shift rename.
Add a visible label or aria-label/tooltip 'Cancel Shift' on the icon-only cancel button on the employee shift card.
critical_code_review_comments: shifts.py join_shift: 'now_local' is set to UTC time — comment already flags this. Late detection uses UTC hour/minute vs the shift's local start_time which can produce false late/overtime results depending on server timezone.
shifts.py end_shift: overtime_minutes uses same UTC-vs-local mismatch as above.

shifts.py: after end_shift, the shift status is reset to 'scheduled' unconditionally, but a shift in 'cancelled' state (unlikely path since cancel is blocked from joining) or beyond effective_to date is not considered.
auth.py register bug (above): response.set_cookie in admin-initiated register overrides caller cookies — real defect.
notifications.py: no pagination beyond hard-coded 50 limit; mark_read returns success even when notif_id is invalid or belongs to another user (no 404).
payroll.py compute_employee_period_stats: leave_days sums approved leaves that overlap the month but counts full 'days' field even if leave spans multiple months (double counting possible).
payroll.py list_payroll: employee branch (query['user_id']=user['_id']) works, but no auth check that user_id filter can only be applied by admins.
shifts.py: no validation that days_of_week values are between 1-7 or that start_time < end_time or effective_from <= effective_to.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all primary flows OK, 2 minor label/UX findings)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file backend/tests/test_shifts_payroll_notifications.py should be reused. Run with `pytest backend/tests/test_shifts_payroll_notifications.py -o addopts=''` to disable xdist (needed because pytest.ini enables loadscope which caused fixture-sharing issues across workers). Key defect: /auth/register overwrites the caller's cookies. If main agent fixes it, re-run the same suite — no changes needed on the test side.
rca_of_the_issue: auth.py register handler always calls response.set_cookie(access_token, refresh_token) with the newly-created user's tokens. When the current user is an admin (the only allowed caller in the new lockdown), those cookies are attached to the admin's browser session because they're same-origin cookies on the same response, causing the admin to be silently switched to the new employee identity. Mitigation: guard the set_cookie block with `if current is None` (i.e., only for anonymous public sign-up). Since anonymous sign-up is currently blocked (403), that block effectively becomes dead code and admin-initiated creation is safe.
